```{r}
#pancile to seedlings proxy:
#panciles in year t is a function of the number of panicles in the plot in the year prior
#so to get the transition rate: number of seedlings in t/#panciles year t-1 (PER PLOT - for now)
plot_summary <- dac %>%
  group_by(Plot, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    seedlings_t = sum(stage == "seedling", na.rm = TRUE),
    panicles_t = sum(No.panicles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>% 
  drop_na()
plot_summary <- plot_summary %>% 
  arrange(Plot, Year) %>%
  group_by(Plot) %>%
  mutate(panicles_tminus1 = lag(panicles_t)) %>%
  drop_na() %>% 
 # ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(germ.rate = seedlings_t/panicles_tminus1) %>% 
  filter(is.finite(germ.rate))
```

```{r}
### 1. GROWTH
#gm.su.sp <- lmer(log.no.stemsT1 ~ log.no.stems + spring.mean.temp + summer.tot.precip + (1|Plot) + (1|Year), data = dac, REML = F)
growth <- fixef(gm.su.sp)
#growth intercept
params$growth.int <- growth["(Intercept)"] + growth["summer.tot.precip"] * params$summer.tot.precip + growth["spring.mean.temp"] * params$spring.mean.temp + params$growth_re
#growth slope
params$growth.slope <- growth["log.no.stems"]

growth_var <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(gm.su.sp)) #assumes same variance across all
params$growth.sd <- growth_var[growth_var$grp=="Residual","sdcor"] # growth sd of residuals

### 2. pflower
#fm.prev_spring.mean.temp <- glmer(pflowerT ~ log.no.stems + prev_spring.mean.temp + (1|Plot) + (1|Year), data = dac, family = "binomial")
flowering <- fixef(fm.prev_spring.mean.temp)
#intercept
params$pflow.int<- flowering["(Intercept)"] + flowering["prev_spring.mean.temp"] * params$prev_spring.mean.temp + params$pflower_re
#slope:
params$pflow.slope <- flowering["log.no.stems"]

####################### 3. no.flowers
#poisson.sp.wt.int2 <- glmer(No.panicles ~ log.no.stems*prev_winter.tot.precip + prev_spring.mean.temp+ (1|Plot) + (1|Year), data = subset(dac, pflowerT == "1"), family = "poisson")

panicles <- fixef(poisson.sp.wt.int2)

params$no.flow.int <- panicles["(Intercept)"] +
  panicles["prev_spring.mean.temp"] * params$prev_spring.mean.temp +
  panicles["prev_winter.tot.precip"] * params$prev_winter.tot.precip + params$no.flow_re

params$no.flow.slope <- panicles["log.no.stems"] +
  panicles["log.no.stems:prev_winter.tot.precip"] * params$prev_winter.tot.precip

### 4. sm.wt.sp.int <- glmer(survT1 ~ log.no.stems*prev_spring.mean.temp + winter.mean.min.temp + (1|Plot) + (1|Year), data = dac.surv, family = "binomial")
```

```{r}
###~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

#SURVIVAL AT SIZE X
s.x=function(x,params) {
	u=exp(params$surv.int+params$surv.slope*x)
	return(u/(1+u))
}

#how to test this: 
### run function for a plant of size 1 and for the first row of parameters
#s.x(x = 1, params = params[1,])
### run function for a plant of size 1 but for all rows of parameters (so get a list )
#s.x(x = 1, params = params)
#ok this works and seems to work for all rows of params. great.

#GROWTH FROM SIZE X TO Y; 
  ## returns a *probability density distribution* for each x value
g.yx<-function(y,x,params){
    # eviction here...
  xb=pmin(pmax(x,minRealsize),maxRealsize) #Transforms all values below/above limits in min/max size (floor & ceiling)
  growth_to_newsize <-params$growth.int + params$growth.slope*xb
  growth_sd <- params$growth.sd
  return(dnorm(y,mean=growth_to_newsize,sd=growth_sd))
  #dnorm(y,mean=params$growth.int + params$growth.slope*x,sd=params$growth.sd)
}

#Tom Miller's combined s and g kernel
P <- function(y, x, params){
  s.x(x, params)*g.yx(y, x, params)
}

#PROBABILITY OF FLOWERING OF SIZE X individuals
pf.x <-function(x,params){
	u<-exp(params$pflow.int+params$pflow.slope*x)
	return(u/(1+u))
}
#testing this for a plant of size 5
#pf.x(x = 8,params = params_expanded)

f.yx <- function(x,params) { 		
  return(pf.x(x,params)*exp(params$no.flow.int+params$no.flow.slope*x)* params$pest)
}
##so this should be outputting the number of new plants made? Yes. pflower * how many flowers made * p(panicle making seedling)
#f.yx(x = 7,params = params_original)


##do big plants make a million flowers?
#exp(params$no.flow.int+params$no.flow.slope*8) 
## no they make a reasonable amount

#SIZE DISTRIBUTION OF RECRUITS - so the ones going from the continuous into the continuous stage. 
recruit.size<-function(y,params){
    ## returns a *probability density distribution*
  dnorm(y,mean=params$recruit.size.mean,sd=params$recruit.size.sd)
}
```

```{r}
params_list <-  filter(params) %>% split(., seq(nrow(.))) #this splits up params into X rows, which I can feed into the function below

###
mat.size = 100 #dimensions of continuous matrix
bigmatrix <- function(params_list, mat.size){

  n <- mat.size
  L <- min.size
  U <- max.size

  # mesh
  h <- (U - L) / n
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n+1)])

  # Fertility matrix
  Fmat <- matrix(0, n, n)

  # recruits of size y from parent size x
  Fmat <- outer(y, y, function(y,x){
    f.yx(x, params_list) * recruit.size(y, params_list)
  }) * h

  # Growth/survival
  Tmat <- t(outer(y, y, P, params = params_list)) * h

  # Full kernel
  IPMmat <- Fmat + Tmat

  out_matrix <- list(
    IPMmat = IPMmat,
    Fmat = Fmat,
    Tmat = Tmat,
    meshpts = y)

  out_lamb <- data.frame(
    Year = params_list$Year,
    lambda = lambda(IPMmat),
    prev_spring.mean.temp = params_list$prev_spring.mean.temp,
    winter.mean.min.temp = params_list$winter.mean.min.temp,
    summer.tot.precip = params_list$summer.tot.precip,
    spring.mean.temp = params_list$spring.mean.temp,
    prev_winter.tot.precip= params_list$prev_winter.tot.precip)

return(list(
  IPMmat = IPMmat,
  Fmat = Fmat,
  Tmat = Tmat,
  meshpts = y,
  lambda = out_lamb))
}

#what I want returned is lambdas
lamb_lists <- lapply(X = params_list, FUN = bigmatrix, mat.size = mat.size) #for each row of params_list, run the big matrix function!

#great~! now make it a df
results <- lapply(params_list, bigmatrix, mat.size = mat.size)

dac_lambda <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results, function(x) x$lambda))

kernels <- lapply(results, function(x) x$IPMmat)
kernel_info <- params %>%
  select(Year)
```

```{r  sim}


stochastic_lambda <- function(kernels, T = 100, burn = 1) { #run the simulation for 50 years

  n <- nrow(kernels[[1]])

  # initial population - this is a nomralized pop, so doesnt matter the absolute amount
  N <- rep(1, n)
  N <- N / sum(N) 

  log_growth <- numeric(T)

  for (t in seq_len(T)) {

    # sample one year's kernel
    K <- kernels[[sample.int(length(kernels), 1)]] #equal change of each kernel being selected

    N_next <- K %*% N #multiplied pop vector by the selected kernel

    log_growth[t] <- log(sum(N_next)) #get lambda by n/nt+1

    N <- N_next / sum(N_next)
  }

  exp(mean(log_growth[(burn + 1):T]))
}
```

```{r}
stochastic_sim <- function(kernels, T = 1000) {

  n <- nrow(kernels[[1]])

  N <- rep(1, n)
  N <- N / sum(N)

  pop_size <- numeric(T + 1)
  pop_size[1] <- sum(N)

  kernel_used <- integer(T)

  for (t in seq_len(T)) {

    k <- sample.int(length(kernels), 1)
    kernel_used[t] <- k

    N <- kernels[[k]] %*% N
    pop_size[t + 1] <- sum(N)
  }

  # list(
  #   pop_size = pop_size,
  #   kernels = kernel_used
  # )
  return(pop_size)
}
sim <- stochastic_sim(kernels, T = 100) #runs that function once

sims <- replicate(
  100,
  stochastic_sim(kernels, T = 100)
)

dim(sims)

  x = 0:100,
  y = sims,

  ylab = "Population size"
)
```
